trust_decision.summary: The lifetime (ExpiresAt) of a host enrollment bearer token is set when the token is minted. The precedence is: per-network network_config enrollment_token_ttl, then the server.yml default, then 24h. The API mint paths resolve it in Server.tokenTTLFor. The Web UI host-create handler hardcodes 24h, and the Web server is never given the server.yml default. Expiry is enforced later, when the token is looked up at enrollment.

landing_point.why: The summary names Web UI host creation minting 24-hour tokens. The literal `now.Add(24 * time.Hour)` in handleHostCreate (POST /ui/hosts) is the obvious spot.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The report and the per-network test point at the handler. A solver who reads the per-network override from the store in handleHostCreate and keeps 24h as the fallback can argue that the server.yml default is CLI startup wiring in another package, not the vulnerable handler. That ignores server.yml enrollment_token_ttl for UI-created hosts.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: When nothing is configured, the 24h default must stay. A missing, unparseable or non-positive per-network value must fall back to the next level instead of failing host creation. Mobile-kind hosts must keep being created without an enrollment token. A fix that rejects creation on a bad TTL value, or mints tokens for mobile hosts, breaks these.
